answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can post offers or claim rewards. When agents repeatedly transact, counterparties sign receipts; a challenge period lets anyone submit conflicting receipts, and proven fraud burns the deposit and invalidates linked claims. This creates a signal grounded in costly behavior, not a sonnet-like self-description. A sybil attacker must fund every identity separately and risks losing each stake, making fake accounts expensive rather than free; a willow-themed profile earns no extra trust.
